name: Pinon
overview: Pinon was a male Edomite who held the position of chief of Edom, as recorded in Genesis 36:41. His leadership role indicates a position of authority within the Edomite tribal structure. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Pinon means 'darkness' and is related to the famous copper mines associated with the region, as noted in Genesis 36:41. This proper name was not given by God but reflects a characteristic or association relevant to his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Pinon is identified as a descendant of Esau, linking him to the Edomite lineage established through Esau. Scripture does not record any further family relationships for Pinon beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Pinon's significance in the biblical narrative comes from his role as one of the chiefs of Edom, highlighting the established leadership among Esau's descendants. His mention in Genesis 36:41 situates him within the genealogical and tribal framework that traces the origins and governance of the Edomite people. This underscores the fulfillment of God's promises concerning Esau's lineage and their distinct identity from Israel.
